text: Papa felt so acutely—you know you are not strong, and there must have been such terrible suspense to go through.” “When did he tell you, Margaret?” “Yesterday, only yesterday,” replied Margaret, detecting the jealousy which prompted the inquiry. “Poor papa!”—trying to divert her mother’s thoughts into compassionate sympathy for all her father had gone through. Mrs. Hale raised her head. “What does he mean by having doubts?” she asked. “Surely, he does not mean that he thinks differently—that he knows better than the Church.” Margaret shook her head, and the tears came into her eyes, as her mother touched the bare nerve of her own regret.
